dublinCore.description: LMS, NLMS and RLS identify the same unknown FIR plant from the same noisy data. Learning curves averaged over 1-20 runs, the weight-error norm, and the true versus estimated weights (or frequency response, or coefficient trajectories) let students compare convergence speed, steady-state misadjustment, stability and tracking after a plant change.

learningObjectives: Compare the convergence speed and final MSE of LMS, NLMS and RLS on the same system-identification problem, using the learning curves and the read-out table
Analyze how input correlation, measured by the eigenvalue spread chi(R), slows LMS and NLMS but not RLS
Evaluate the LMS step-size trade-off by predicting the misadjustment mu M sigma_x^2 / 2 and the stability limit, then judging how well each approximation matches the measured values
Evaluate a choice of RLS forgetting factor lambda for tracking, explaining why lambda = 1 fails after the plant changes
Explain why a filter shorter than the plant settles at a floor above the noise power (J_min > sigma_v^2)
prerequisites: Mean-squared error and the Wiener solution
LMS, NLMS and RLS update equations

misconceptions.misconception: Any LMS step size below 2/(M sigma_x^2) is safe
misconceptions.correction: That bound guarantees convergence of the mean weights only; the MSE needs a smaller step, about 2/((M+2) sigma_x^2) for white Gaussian input, and bursts of large input samples can destabilize LMS with correlated input
misconceptions.evidence: With white input and M = 8, 5 of 10 runs diverge at mu = 0.22 and all 10 at mu = 0.23, before the warning at 0.250; with AR(1) a = 0.9 input one run diverges at mu = 0.03

misconceptions.misconception: RLS always tracks faster than LMS
misconceptions.correction: After start-up RLS tracks at a rate set by lambda; at equal misadjustment it recovers no faster than LMS
misconceptions.evidence: After the plant change at n = 500, LMS (mu = 0.01) recovers in 340 iterations and RLS (lambda = 0.99) in 405, both with about 4% misadjustment

misconceptions.misconception: A flat learning curve means the weights are correct
misconceptions.correction: Weight errors along small-eigenvalue directions barely change the output, so the MSE can look converged while the weights are not
misconceptions.evidence: With AR(1) a = 0.9 input the LMS MSE is within 1.6 dB of J_min while its weight error is about -27 dB instead of -45 dB

accessibility.screenReaderScript: System identification with three adaptive filters. LMS (blue), NLMS (green) and RLS (maroon) learn the same unknown FIR plant from the same noisy data. Plots show the learning curves in dB, the weight-error norm, and the true versus estimated weights. Sliders set the noise level, number of averaged runs, filter length, LMS step size, NLMS normalized step size and RLS forgetting factor.

controls.label: Plant
controls.description: Chooses the unknown FIR plant: A (4 taps), B (8-tap lowpass) or C (12-tap echo), each scaled to unit energy

controls.label: Input
controls.description: Chooses a unit-power input: white noise or AR(1) colored noise with a = 0.5 or a = 0.9

controls.label: RLS delta
controls.description: Sets the RLS initialisation P(0) = I / delta

controls.label: Noise power
controls.description: Observation-noise power sigma_v^2 added to the plant output

controls.label: Runs averaged
controls.description: Number of independent runs averaged into the learning curves and read-outs

controls.label: Filter length M
controls.description: Number of taps of all three adaptive filters

controls.label: LMS step size mu
controls.description: LMS step size; the label turns red and a warning appears above 2/(M sigma_x^2)

controls.label: RLS forgetting factor lambda
controls.description: RLS forgetting factor; memory is about 1/(1 - lambda) samples

controls.label: Run / Pause
controls.description: Starts, pauses or resumes the experiment (it opens paused); after it finishes, replays it from n = 0

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Restores all default settings and restarts the experiment

controls.label: Change the plant at n = 500
controls.description: Toggles a sign flip of every plant tap at n = 500 to test tracking

controls.label: Panel
controls.description: Chooses the right-hand panel: true vs estimated weights, frequency response, or coefficient trajectories

visualElements.description: Learning curves: ensemble-averaged MSE in dB versus iteration for LMS, NLMS and RLS, with the Wiener floor J_min dashed
Weight-error norm ||w_o - w[n]||^2 in dB versus iteration for the three algorithms
Right panel: bar chart of true and estimated weights, or frequency responses, or trajectories of the two largest taps (run 1)
Read-out table: final MSE, measured and approximate misadjustment, convergence or recovery iteration, J_min, eigenvalue spread and the LMS bound

model.description: System identification: d[n] = w_o^T x[n] + v[n] with a unit-energy FIR plant, unit-power white or AR(1) input and white Gaussian noise. LMS, NLMS and RLS run on identical seeded data for 1500 iterations; curves are averaged over runs and 5-iteration blocks.
equations: LMS: w <- w + mu e[n] x[n]
NLMS: w <- w + mu~ e[n] x[n] / (eps + ||x[n]||^2)
RLS: k = P x / (lambda + x^T P x); w <- w + k e[n]; P <- (P - k x^T P) / lambda; P(0) = I / delta
LMS misadjustment ~ mu M sigma_x^2 / 2; NLMS ~ mu~ / (2 - mu~); RLS ~ (1 - lambda) M / (1 + lambda)
J_min = sigma_v^2 + sigma_y^2 - p^T R_M^{-1} p
algorithms: Cyclic Jacobi eigenvalue method for the eigenvalue spread
limitations: The misadjustment approximations assume small steps and long filters
Error powers above +40 dB are clipped in the averages
The plant change is a sign flip of all taps

instructionalStrategies: Controlled comparison on identical random data
Comparing measured misadjustment with textbook approximations
extensions: Add an affine-projection algorithm between NLMS and RLS
